name: Pelican Acquisition Corporation (Rights) — Delisted / Converted to Greenland Energy Company (GLND)

profile.description: PELIR was the Nasdaq ticker for the rights issued by Pelican Acquisition Corporation, a blank-check SPAC. Each right entitled the holder to receive one-tenth of one ordinary share upon completion of a business combination. Pelican's shareholders approved the merger with Greenland Exploration Limited and March GL Company on March 19, 2026, and the combination closed on March 25, 2026, forming Greenland Energy Company. Nasdaq filed a Form 25-NSE the same day removing PELIR (along with PELI ordinary shares and PELIU units) from listing. PELIR no longer exists as an independently tradable security — any residual rights converted into shares of the successor, which now trades under ticker GLND.

investment_thesis: There is no investable thesis for PELIR. The security was the rights component of Pelican Acquisition Corporation, a blank-check SPAC that completed its business combination with Greenland Exploration Limited and March GL Company on March 25, 2026, forming Greenland Energy Company [2]. Nasdaq filed a Form 25-NSE the same day, formally delisting PELIR, PELI, and PELIU from the exchange [1]. Per the rights' terms, each PELIR right converted into one-tenth of one ordinary share of the successor entity at the merger close, meaning any economic value associated with the original rights now resides in Greenland Energy Company shares (NASDAQ: GLND, trading around $2.31 as of early August 2026), not in the extinct PELIR ticker [2][3].
thesis_continued: For IOWN screening purposes, PELIR should be treated as a dead ticker: there is no current price, no trading volume, and no operating business associated with it. Any residual quoting services still listing PELIR (e.g., legacy OTC ticker pages) reflect stale historical data rather than an active market. Investors seeking exposure to the underlying Greenland Jameson Land Basin exploration story — a fully-funded two-well drilling program targeting an October 2026 start, with Greenland Energy earning a 70% project interest alongside partner 80 Mile's 30% — must do so through the successor ticker GLND directly, which would require its own independent IOWN screen rather than treatment as a continuation of PELIR [3]. This report should be considered closed out / retired from the active screening universe.
